newsitem.title: USA: US CREDIT OUTLOOK--June Producer Price Index (PPI).
newsitem.headline: US CREDIT OUTLOOK--June Producer Price Index (PPI).

text.p: The U.S. June Producer Price Index (PPI) is likely to set a positive tone for U.S. government securities trading on Friday.
The PPI, due at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT on Friday, is expected to be flat for June, and up 0.1 percent without its more volatile food and energy components, economists said.
"There's no expectation of any problem with the PPI," said Elliott Platt, managing director of economic research at Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette.
"Everyone's locked into the notion that it will be unchanged, with the core up 0.1 pct," he said.
Platt said some investors might be disappointed that the PPI series has stopped declining. It has declined in each of the last five months, including a 0.3 percent drop in May.
But Platt said, "I think it should be a fine number for the market."
Still, the question is whether a favorable PPI report can help the market to move higher at this point.
"I would think not," said Platt, "pretty much because the market has been trading on this low inflation scenario."
Platt said the market would benefit more from evidence that the economy is continuing to grow more slowly than it would from one more report pointing to low inflation.
Richard Koss, economist at Maria Fiorini Ramirez Inc., said the market might suffer more from a sharper-than-expected rise in the June PPI than it might benefit from benign data.
After a friendly report, investors might take some profits "after such a stupendous rally," Koss said.
And if the PPI were less friendly than expected, "the market could have a bad day," Platt said.
But Anthony Karydakis, senior financial economist at First Chicago Capital Markets Inc., said the market is ready to move higher, given an excuse to do so.
"I expect the PPI to look good to the market," he said. "It's a close call as to whether it will show its sixth consecutive monthly decline, which would be unprecedented."
Whether the PPI is down, flat, or up 0.1 percent, the market will still be working with a strong premise of extremely well controlled inflation, Karydakis said.
"If the PPI declines, it will give the market an excuse to launch another an assault on 6-1/2 percent," he said.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond ended at 100-23/32 on Thursday to yield 6.57 percent.
Karydakis said the risk to the market on the PPI was assymetric.

"If the PPI rises modestly, the market won't get hurt that much," he said. "Nobody is going to think that you have something wrong with the inflation picture if you get a 0.1 percent or 0.2 percent increase after five straight months of declines. It doesn't work that way."
Karydakis said the market was in "excellent" shape.
"The market has shown a tremendous amount of resilience over the last few days and is looking for an excuse to move higher," he said.
Dealers indicated that Federal funds would open at 5-7/16 percent on Friday.
